subject: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Price <joanna.price@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model

Hi Joanna — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we discussed: 

Summary of call / assumptions
- Expected steady-state volume: ~120M tokens / month (models: mix of chat + completion; estimated prompt:completion ratio ~30:70).
- Average tokens per API call (end-user request): ~460 tokens.
- Target price range you called out: $200k–$300k ARR (you mentioned procurement to validate).
- Primary use: product features with low-latency SLOs; we recommended pinned dedicated pools + prefix caching for common prompts.

Unit economics and ask from Acme
- Target unit metric: $/1M tokens (you asked for a target of <$200 / 1M tokens as a ballpark).
- Key levers we will model: committed volume discounts, quantization profile, batching, prefix/KV cache hit-rate (we modeled 15–40% effective reduction in billed tokens depending on pattern).

Attachments (initial artifacts)
- ACME_cost_model_Q4_v2.xlsx — cost model workbook with monthly burn and sensitivity tabs (attached).
- redwood_pricing_calculator.csv — simplified pricing calculator (attached).

Requested next steps
1) Confirm monthly token target and ideal contract term (12 vs 24 months).
2) Share procurement contact + billing info.
3) We'll follow up with an invoice estimate and a one-page cost breakdown for your CFO.

I'll send an updated estimate after you confirm the monthly volume.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ACME_cost_model_Q4_v2.xlsx (XLSX)
Attachment: redwood_pricing_calculator.csv (CSV)
From: Joanna Price <joanna.price@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-26T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model

Thanks Sean — good notes and appreciate the artifacts. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed monthly target: ~120M tokens / month (steady-state expected after Q1 ramp).
- Budget range for inference: roughly $200k–$300k ARR — we'd like the estimate to fit inside that window if possible.
- Key ask from procurement: line-item invoice with committed vs overage pricing, and the effective cost per 1M tokens at expected usage.

Also looping in Tom (engineering lead) and procurement so they can review the technical and billing pieces. Please include SOC 2 attestation link in the next email for our security team.

If you can send an updated invoice estimate and a short one-page cost breakdown that maps to our $/1M target, we can move this to procurement review next week.

Best,
Joanna Price
Head of Product
Acme Corp

Date: 2026-11-27T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model (updated)

Joanna / Tom / procurement — attaching an updated invoice estimate and a condensed cost breakdown that maps to your $/1M target and requested line items. Key highlights below.

Attachments included
- ACME_invoice_estimate_Nov27.pdf — one-page invoice estimate with committed volume pricing, overage rates, and billing terms.
- ACME_cost_model_Q4_v2.xlsx (updated) — includes sensitivity tab for cache hit-rate and batching assumptions.

Top-line estimate (steady-state, 120M tokens / month)
- List price (no commit): $220 / 1M tokens -> monthly invoice at list = $26,400.
- Proposed committed rate (12-month, 120M tokens/mo): 35% committed discount -> $143 / 1M tokens -> monthly = $17,160 -> annualized = $205,920.
- Effective unit economics with cache/batching (modeled 25% effective billed token reduction): effective $/1M tokens ~ $107 -> projected annual spend ~ $155k.

Line items on the attached estimate
- Committed token blocks (monthly)
- Overage rate per 1M tokens after committed block
- Dedicated pool baseline surcharge (for pinned low-latency SLOs) — one-time onboarding fee shown separately
- Support/observability add-on (optional)

Notes / assumptions
- Cache hit-rate assumed: 25% (we included a 15–40% sensitivity sheet). If your prompt patterns have lower reuse, final effective cost will be higher.
- Quantization/instance sizing assumptions are in the workbook; we can run a quick trial to validate effective throughput and KV hit-rate.

Next steps
1) Please confirm you want the 12-month committed quote at the proposed committed block.
2) If yes, share procurement contact + billing PO and we'll generate an SOW/DocuSign packet.
3) Rishi and Marissa, can you please add SOC 2 link and the standard SAML/KMS integration notes to the packet?

Thanks — I added the one-page PDF as requested for CFO review.

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_invoice_estimate_Nov27.pdf (PDF), ACME_cost_model_Q4_v2.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Joanna Price <joanna.price@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-28T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model (approved to proceed to procurement)

Thanks Sean — this looks good and aligns with the budget window we discussed. We want to move to procurement review: please send the SOW/DocuSign and include SOC 2 attestation and our requested billing term (Net-30).

Procurement contact is procurement@acme.com (cc'ed). Tom, Joanna, and procurement team will review the one-pager and the workbook this afternoon. If procurement is happy, we'll sign the committed 12-month block.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — please loop in Marissa for billing questions.

Best,
Joanna
Head of Product
Acme Corp
